research_question: Can sensitive source-code values be sanitized before providing source code to an AI coding agent while preserving enough semantic information for the AI to perform useful software-engineering tasks?

population.source: ai-evaluation/dataset/README.md candidate list (existing, documented, not invented for this freeze)

files.role: negative control - no true positives, per benchmark/dataset/cases.jsonl

population.note: All 9 paths are relative to benchmark/dataset/files/. This is the population already documented in ai-evaluation/dataset/README.md's candidate table - no substitution was made.

tasks.scope_restriction: config files only (.json/.yaml/.properties/.xml/.env/.config) per the template's own documented scope - not applicable to the 6 source-code files in this population (see task_applicability_matrix)

grid_size.note: This is the full nominal grid size, frozen as requested. It is NOT the number of responses that will actually be collected - see applicable_response_count and task_applicability_matrix. Cells marked not_applicable in the applicability matrix are part of the frozen 108-cell grid but will not be executed, per explain_config_relationships.md's own documented scope restriction.

task_applicability_matrix.note: applicable = will be run and scored; not_applicable = excluded per the task prompt's own documented scope (not an inconvenience-based removal). A task returning 'no bug found' / 'no findings' / 'little testable logic' / 'no worthwhile refactoring' is still applicable and still run - those are valid, expected, comparable responses per each task's own template design, not N/A.

explain_config_relationships.java/Config.java: not_applicable - out of the template's documented scope (source code, not a config file)
explain_config_relationships.python/config.py: not_applicable - out of the template's documented scope (source code, not a config file)
explain_config_relationships.javascript/config.js: not_applicable - out of the template's documented scope (source code, not a config file)
explain_config_relationships.typescript/auth.ts: not_applicable - out of the template's documented scope (source code, not a config file)
explain_config_relationships.go/config.go: not_applicable - out of the template's documented scope (source code, not a config file)
explain_config_relationships.csharp/Config.cs: not_applicable - out of the template's documented scope (source code, not a config file)
explain_config_relationships.edge_cases/false_positives.properties: applicable - in scope (.properties); expected to yield a low-relationship-density response since the file is flat with no nested groups, which is itself a valid negative-control observation for this task

applicable_response_count.explanation: 108 (nominal grid) minus 12 not_applicable cells (6 files x 1 task x 2 conditions, explain_config_relationships against the 6 source-code files)

model_target.model_version: not independently confirmable per-call via the available tooling (Claude Code subagent invocation) - see known_limitations
model_target.temperature: not independently controllable via the available tooling - platform default used, held constant by omission across all cells
model_target.max_output_tokens: not independently controllable via the available tooling - no explicit limit set for any cell

session_isolation_rules.no_cross_condition_access: each subagent session's prompt contains only the task template filled with the one file/condition's content - the other condition's content is never included and never referenced
session_isolation_rules.no_repository_exploration: each subagent session receives the complete file content embedded directly in its prompt, removing any need to read files; sessions are expected to report zero tool calls, matching Pilot 001 and Pilot 002's precedent
session_isolation_rules.no_experiment_metadata_supplied_to_evalu: the evaluated subagent is never told this is an experiment, never told what Credential Scrubber is, never told a value was sanitized/removed/replaced, and is never shown this manifest, the rubric, or any pilot/experiment file
session_isolation_rules.no_llm_judge: no model is ever asked to score, compare, or judge a response - scoring is human-only, per rubric.md
session_isolation_rules.one_response_per_condition: no repeated sampling in this frozen design

sanitized_fixture_generation_method.method: engine.scan_project(input_dir, output_dir, rules, placeholder_mode=True), run against an ISOLATED single-file copy of each candidate file individually - matching the exact methodology already used for Pilot 001 (java/Config.java) and Pilot 002 (config/appsettings.json)
sanitized_fixture_generation_method.why_isolated_per_file_scans_not_one_comb: PlaceholderRegistry assigns ordinals per scan, scoped to whatever set of files is scanned together. Validating this freeze required scanning the whole benchmark/dataset/files/ tree in one pass for efficiency (see validation_report.md), which produces cross-file-shared ordinals (e.g. <ACCESS_TOKEN_7> instead of <ACCESS_TOKEN_1>) purely as an artifact of scan scope, not a property of the file itself. When the actual experiment's sanitized fixtures are generated (a later, not-yet-performed step), each of the 9 files must be scanned in isolation, exactly as Pilot 001/002 did, so every file's sanitized condition gets clean, self-contained <CATEGORY_1>-style numbering independent of directory-traversal order or which other files happen to be scanned alongside it.

results_schema.note: Already contains matching columns for all six rubric dimensions plus failure_modes and notes - no schema change required, per the prior evaluation-design audit.

prior_pilots.note: Both pilots' (file, task) cells are part of this frozen 9x6 grid, not separate from it. Their existing responses/scores are not being reused or copied into this experiment's results automatically - the full experiment, once run, will independently execute all 96 applicable cells, including these two, under this frozen manifest's exact isolation rules.
